newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. January durable goods and weekly jobless claims data, dealers said on Thursday.
Durable goods figures for January are forecast to show an increase of 1.5 percent compared with a 1.9 percent decline reported in December.
Weekly jobless claims for the week ended February 22 are expected to rise to 310,000 against the previous week's 309,000.
"The market was marked up slightly across the board today on some speculative position adjustments," a local dealer said.
"Some people are waiting for tonight's release of the durable goods and weekly jobless claims figures, for fresh clues to market direction," he said.
"The numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions, so I don't think there will be much impact," he added.
In day-to-day rates, Thursday/Friday rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent but weekend and week-fixed rose 1/8 point each to a common 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, respectively.

Among longer dates, two-months rose 1/16 point to 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, four-months rose 1/8 point to 5-9/16 5-7/16, six-months rose 1/16 point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 and twelve-months rose 1/8 point to 5-7/8 5-3/4 percent.
